source.title: WaterDrum: Watermarking for Data-centric Unlearning Metric
source.authors: Xin-Yang Lu; Xin-Yuan Niu; G. Lau; N. Bui; Rachael Hwee Ling Sim; John Russell Himawan; Fan-Yu Wen; Chuan-Sheng Foo; See-Kiong Ng; B. Low

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates data-centric unlearning metrics and benchmarks algorithms for removing data-owner influence. It does not test recovery of targeted knowledge by the attacks in the claim. Its discussion of jailbreaks, relearning, and latent knowledge extraction refers to other work.
record.gate_note: The paper's own experiments measure watermark-based data influence and metric properties, not near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery after unlearning. It explicitly distinguishes data-influence removal from concept or knowledge unlearning. Adversarial attacks and their results are discussed as prior work, not tested here. Rows below record the paper's own qualitative benchmark results on unlearning algorithms; they do not test versions A–F.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a watermark-based data-influence metric and benchmarks unlearning algorithms on it. It runs no recovery attack: no relearning, no activation ablation, no quantization, no prompting attack. It does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance. It explicitly separates data-influence removal from knowledge unlearning. Its mentions of jailbreaks and relearning (Lynch et al., Wang et al.) are cited prior work. The benchmark rows measure watermark signal on the forget set, a different construct from version A's near-chance knowledge accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors propose WaterDrum and show it alone meets their separability and calibration desiderata under similar data. A preliminary benchmark shows the tested algorithms stay far from retraining. They draw no conclusion about knowledge recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a watermark-based unlearning metric; it does not reproduce or test the claim's recovery-attack recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different unlearning outcomes across methods and data-similarity settings; its algorithm benchmark is presented for WaterDrum-Ax and is extended to multiple owners and exact-duplicate settings in Sec. H.3.

fits_no_version.finding: On the WaterDrum-Ax watermark metric, KL and Task Vector remove forget-set influence but also lose much retain-set influence. GD and SCRUB keep some retain influence but leave forget influence. No method approaches retraining. The pattern recurs with 1, 3 and 5 owners and in the exact-duplicate setting (Sec. H.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-influence unlearning methods trade forget-set removal against retain-set preservation, measured by watermark signal rather than knowledge accuracy.

record.problems: The algorithm benchmark is preliminary, and its reported Fig. 4 outcomes are not numerically stated in the text. Experiments use data-centric unlearning rather than targeted-knowledge unlearning and do not include the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted for metric comparisons, separability/calibration tests, or WaterDrum's robustness tests because those measure metric performance or watermark resilience rather than recovery of targeted knowledge after unlearning. The additional multi-owner algorithm plots in Sec. H.3 were not separately extracted; they repeat the qualitative method pattern reported in Sec. 5.1 under different owner counts and data-similarity settings.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance, no general-capability benchmark, no simple recovery attack.
No activation ablation or mechanism analysis.
No prompting, jailbreak or in-context recovery.
No method claimed robust to these attacks.

record.verdict_notes: This is a metric paper about data-owner influence removal (watermark verification), not knowledge unlearning or recovery attacks. The resilience tests in Sec. D concern attacks on the watermark metric by a model owner, not recovery of unlearned knowledge. They bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy, general capability evaluation, or simple recovery attack after unlearning.
No recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion as a mechanism.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery tests.
No newer unlearning method is tested for resistance to the recovery attacks in the claim.
